blurb: Massive Brazilian mastiff with loose skin, pronounced dewlaps and a sloping-up topline
description: The Fila Brasileiro is a large Brazilian mastiff-type guard dog with thick, loose skin and a short dense coat; ownership is restricted in some countries.
answer: The Fila Brasileiro is a large mastiff-type working dog from Brazil, used as a guard dog, for cattle herding and for big-game hunting. It stands about 60 to 75 cm tall, weighs at least 40 kg in bitches and more in males, and is known for its thick, loose skin and heavy build.

body: The breed is thought to descend from European dogs brought to Brazil during the colonial period, with little or no influence from native South American dogs. It was raised mainly on large plantations and cattle farms, where it worked with cattle and hunted jaguars, and in the 18th century it was also used to track escaped slaves. Its name comes from the Portuguese filar, to hold or grab, marking it as a catch dog.

The first written standard appeared in 1946, and Paulo Santos Cruz, regarded as the father of the breed, bred it systematically. Today three Brazilian clubs maintain different standards, and owning the breed is banned or restricted in several countries, including the United Kingdom and Australia.

The Fila resembles a larger, stockier Bloodhound, with low-hanging ears and a big, heavy head. Its skin is thick and loose, forming pronounced dewlaps at the neck, and unusually the croup sits higher than the withers. The short, dense coat is usually fawn, black or brindle, sometimes with a black mask; white markings are limited under the FCI standard.

faq.q: Is the Fila Brasileiro banned in some countries?
faq.a: Yes. Ownership requires a court exemption in countries including the United Kingdom, Norway and Australia, and it is illegal to own and breed in Turkey.

faq.q: How big does a Fila Brasileiro get?
faq.a: Males stand about 65 to 75 cm and weigh at least 50 kg; bitches are slightly smaller at about 60 to 70 cm and at least 40 kg.

faq.q: Is the Fila Brasileiro recognised by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 225 in Group 2, with Brazil as the country of origin.
